thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty incident PD-9821 triggered: prod-lb-targets-unhealthy-us-west-2 (LB target health degraded + TLS handshake errors). Auto-page to SRE oncall.

pagerduty: Incident PD-9821 | prod-lb-targets-unhealthy-us-west-2
pagerduty: Trigger reason: ALB target_health_count > 30% unhealthy across target group tg-web-frontend-usw2
pagerduty: Symptoms: 502/523 errors, TLS handshake failures observed at ALB layer.

Maya: I'm oncall, acked PD and joining. Looking into health checks and cert errors first.

Sanjay: I'll pull up ALB target status and recent deploys. No deploys in the last 45m from CI.

Maya: Thanks. Observing spike in TLS alert logs:\n```
ALB: TLS handshake failure: unsupported protocol (client hello) from 54.127.21.9:46302
TargetHealth: Unhealthy threshold exceeded for target i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6
```

Maya: Rolling a quick `curl` against the ALB shows intermittent TLS handshake failures and some backends 502.

Emily: Are customers seeing 5xx in dashboard? Support flagged a small increase in error rate for POST /v1/generate in US-WEST-2. Not yet a worldwide outage.

Kiana: DNS check — we pushed a small DNS alias change for canary routing earlier today to route legacy hostnames through a new ALB. Might be related if some clients hit legacy hostnames and get mismatched TLS cert. Checking route53 records and alias target.

Maya: Good call. If cert mismatch for legacy hostname -> ALB serving certificate for new domain might cause handshake failures for SNI mismatch. Can someone check the certificate the ALB is presenting?

Sanjay: Pulling cert via openssl on one of the frontend ALBs:
```
openssl s_client -connect prod-web-alb-usw2-012345.us-west-2.elb.amazonaws.com:443 -servername legacy.redwood.ai
```
Sanjay: Cert is for `*.redwood.ai` but SAN list doesn't include `legacy.redwood.ai` (we consolidated certs last month). That explains SNI mismatch for legacy hostnames.

Maya: That would produce TLS handshake failures. Impact scope: clients using legacy.redwood.ai (internal migration not fully completed). Do we have a quick mitigation?

Kiana: Two options: 1) Add legacy.redwood.ai to cert SAN and deploy (takes ~10-15m to issue/attach), or 2) Update Route53 alias to route legacy hostnames to the old ALB that still has the legacy cert for a temporary period. Option 2 is faster to propagate but DNS TTLs vary.

Ops Runbook Bot: Runbook suggestion: `route LegacyHostname -> previous-alb` (quick rollback) OR `attach cert with SAN` (deploy cert to ALB). See runbook id RB-12 for TLS SNI issues.

Maya: Let's do the rollback to old ALB first to reduce customer impact, while Kiana starts cert issuance in parallel. I can coordinate DNS change.

Kiana: Changing alias now to point legacy.redwood.ai -> old-alb-usw2 (previously standby). Making the Route53 change:\n```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"legacy.redwood.ai.","Type":"A","AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZLW-OLDBAL","DNSName":"old-alb-usw2-abcdef.elb.amazonaws.com","EvaluateTargetHealth":false}}}]}'
```
Kiana: Change submitted. Change id C0A1B2C3. Propagation ETA variable (check `dig`).

Sanjay: Starting to drain problematic targets in the new ALB target group to reduce 502s:
```
aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:elasticloadbalancing:...:tg-web-frontend-usw2 --targets Id=i-0a1b2c3d4e5f6
```
Sanjay: Deregistered a few flapping instances to see if steady state improves.

Maya: Good. Emily, can you update support slack thread and status page that we're mitigating with DNS rollback and draining flapping targets? Mark impact as "partial degradation — some US-WEST-2 traffic may see TLS errors/5xx".

Emily: Updating status. Notifying top-10 affected customers via support playbook.

Kiana: Cert issuance started with CA. Request ID CA-5567. ETA ~12min for SAN update (+ALB attach). I'll post when the cert is ready.

pagerduty: PD-9821 auto-escalation scheduled in 8m if not acknowledged by escalation policy.

Maya: DNS change propagated to a large portion of clients in ~4 minutes; error rates dropping from 18% to 3% for US-WEST-2. Monitoring.

Sanjay: Backend 502s down; target group healthy percent rising to 95%. Looks like draining flappers helped.

Kiana: Cert is issued. Attaching to new ALB now (can update ALB listener certificate):\n```
aws elbv2 modify-listener --listener-arn arn:aws:elbv2:...:listener/abc --certificates CertificateArn=arn:aws:acm:us-west-2:123456:certificate/abcd
```
Kiana: Certificate attached. Verifying SNI now.

Maya: Verified via curl with SNI header — legacy.redwood.ai now gets proper cert and TLS handshake succeeded from multiple vantage points. Error rate back to baseline.

Emily: Status page updated: incident mitigated, partial customer impact resolved. Postmortem will include rollout of consolidated cert and missed legacy SAN in cert policy.

Maya: Oncall handoff at +2h: I'll summarize in incident report and hand over to SRE rotation for post-incident follow-up.

Sanjay: Adding note: we need a guard in deploy pipelines to ensure SAN coverage when consolidating hostnames. Also recommend lowering Route53 TTL during migrations.

Kiana: Will create follow-up ticket with ACME team to add automated SAN checks.

Ops Runbook Bot: Incident resolved (RB-12 suggested steps applied). Please run the postmortem template and tag `blameless` and `severity:high` if customer escalations occurred.

Maya: Thanks everyone. Closing PD and incident thread. :white_check_mark:
